about: Latin as the Church sings it, read from its spelling (latin.js): the ecclesiastical, Italianate pronunciation as the Liber Usualis gives it, its e and o open throughout (research/VOCALWIND_CHOIR.md, "Latin"; the owner, 15 November 2026). `vowels`: each vowel letter's sound, and the digraphs sung as one vowel (ae, oe) or one syllable (au; eu only where a word begins with it, eu and ui in the `monosyllables`). `consonants`: each consonant letter's sound where no rule below changes it. `soft`: c, g, sc and xc before a front vowel (`front`: e, i, y, ae, oe). `digraphs`: two letters one sound (gn [ɲ]; h after c, p, t, r). `h_as_k`: the words whose h is sung [k]. `ex_voiced`: a word's opening ex before a vowel or h sung [ɡz]; x before s is [ks], the s its own (exsúltet). `ti_before_vowel`: t before an unstressed i that a vowel follows, unless s, t or x is before it. `n_before_velar`: n before [k] or [ɡ]. A syllable takes the one consonant before its vowel, or two where they are a mute and a liquid (`mutes`, `liquids`) or a consonant and [w] (qu, gu). Stress: the vowel printed with an acute (á, é, ǽ: the liturgical books print it on every word of three syllables or more), else where the books print it most (scripts/download-latin-lexicon.mjs), else the penult of two syllables, else the penult where it is long (a macron, a digraph) or closed (gn, and sc before a front vowel, one sound of two letters, close it as two consonants do: insígnis, Francísci), else the antepenult -- where the penult is open on a plain vowel, by that vowel's length in Wiktionary's Latin where it has the word, else a guess, said. `durations`: the phone whose Klatt duration each sound is timed by (durations.js; no Latin measurement read yet), its sound kept as its own.
sources: Benedictines of Solesmes, Liber Usualis (Tournai: Desclée, 1961), "Rules for the pronunciation of Latin": e and o open in every syllable (EWTN's table adapted from it, https://www.ewtn.com/catholicism/answers/latin-ecclesiastical-24788; ACDA's Choral Journal on Roman Latin, its e [ɛ] and o [ɔ])
research/VOCALWIND_CHOIR.md, "Latin": the rules approved without a design (c and g soft before e, i, ae, oe; gn [ɲ]; ti before a vowel [tsi]; sc before e, i [ʃ]; qu [kw]; h silent; ae, oe [ɛ])
